attributes.title: Level 1

subgroups.name: Discover

steps.text: Watch this video to learn about using 2D tilemaps and physics in your projects to create a side-view perspective with sprites that can jump!

questions.hint: Which perspective does the user have in a 2D platformer tilemap?
questions.title: [Select one] For 2D platformers, the user views the world as if looking from ____________.
questions.correctResponse: This 2D perspective allows the user to see the  platforms as well as the space above and below them.

questions.hint: What allows a sprite to jump up to a platform, then fall back down?
questions.title: [Select one] In computer programs, what is needed to code a jump?
questions.correctResponse: Velocity works to push the sprite up in the air, then acceleration pulls it back down to the ground.

questions.hint: Which code block makes a sprite fall back down after it has jumped up?
questions.title: [Select one] In code, gravity can be simulated using what block?
questions.correctResponse: A positive ay (acceleration y) value pulls the sprite back down to the ground.

questions.hint: Do positive or negative vy values cause a sprite to jump up?
questions.title: [Select one] Setting a negative value for vy (velocity y) within an [on button pressed] container will make a sprite jump up when the user presses a button.
questions.correctResponse: The [on button pressed] container will run the code within it when the button is pressed, and a negative vy (velocity y) value decreases the sprite’s y position moving the sprite up the screen.

subgroups.title: 2D Tilemaps and Physics!
subgroups.introduction: Watch this video to learn about using 2D tilemaps and physics in your projects to create a side-view perspective with sprites that can jump!

attributes.description: Welcome to Level 1 of Green Belt! In this level, you’ll learn more about 2D platformer games and physics. In 2D platformers, we see the game as if looking from the side. We can use physics concepts, like velocity and acceleration, to make our sprites jump up onto platforms and avoid obstacles. Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 1:

badges.title: Let’s Get Physics-cal!
badges.description: Use physics to control sprite movement in a platformer-style tilemap project.

badges.title: Hop, Skip, and a Jump
badges.description: Set a sprite’s y-velocity (vy).

badges.title: Defying Gravity
badges.description: Set a sprite’s y-acceleration (ay).

badges.title: Wallflower
badges.description: Check if a sprite is touching a tilemap wall before making something happen in a project.
